sources.title: Deterministic Replay for AI Agent Systems
admitted: Agent execution can be represented as an ordered typed step sequence.
Strict replay should fail rather than fall back to live network when no trace match exists.
Transport replay alone does not capture filesystem or database mutation.
limitations: The evaluation text says five workloads replayed five times yet labels the total n=250; the displayed arithmetic implies 25 unless an unreported factor exists. Numeric results are not admitted.
The exact-output fidelity definition is suitable only for the recorded trace and does not establish task correctness.
Single-author v1 preprint; no independent replication assessed.

sources.title: How Many Tasks Are Enough for Agent Benchmark Decisions? A Replay Analysis of Public LLM Agent Benchmarks
admitted: Partial-evaluation sufficiency requires decision-error, group-coverage, and unresolved/defer targets together.
Unresolved cases remain in the decision-class denominator rather than disappearing.
Threshold, task order, group coverage, decision rule, and unresolved target must be predeclared and reported.
Replay over completed records does not estimate performance on future task draws without a sampling model.
limitations: Reported replay findings are conditional on public completed records, chosen groups, ordered comparison orientation, thresholds, and policies.
Adaptive policies and learned groups may change budgets and require prespecified pilot or historical information.

sources.title: HarnessRisk: A Lifecycle-Oriented Benchmark for Agent Harness Safety
admitted: Operational safety is a joint property of model and harness configuration.
Utility, attack success, persistence, and detection are distinct outcome axes.
Fresh state, mock side effects, full trajectory evidence, and lifecycle-specific controls are useful harness evaluation dimensions.
Their sandbox is explicitly process/configuration isolation, not a kernel namespace, chroot, or firewall boundary.
limitations: Primary labels use a GPT-5.4 evaluator; reported evaluator agreement is imperfect.
Provider failures are filtered, so estimates are conditional on valid runs.
Seed/case dependence is not modeled in reported bootstrap scope.
Cross-harness contrasts are deployed-configuration comparisons, not controlled harness-only causal effects.
